chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the 'Safw' (the best portion) of the wealth. He said: 'It belongs to the Imam, who takes the swift mare, the fine mount, the cutting sword, and the armor, before the booty is distributed. This is the Safw of the wealth.'

key_terms.الْفَارِهَ: Fine, elegant, or proud (referring to a mount)
key_terms.الْقَاطِعَ: Cutting or sharp (referring to a sword)
key_terms.صَفْوُ الْمَالِ: The best portion or select part of the wealth/booty

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Safw al-Mal and what items does the Imam take from the booty?
ai.summary: In this narration from Sahih al-Tusi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that 'Safw al-Mal' refers to the pre-distribution selection of premium military assets—specifically a swift horse, a fine mount, a sharp sword, and armor—by the Imam. This practice underscores the Imam's right to the best portion of spoils to maintain military readiness and leadership prestige, distinct from the general division of wealth among fighters.
